text:
luis: FYI got a customer report from Atrato Health — they see a big latency regression on text-generation since ~09:12 PST. p50 up from ~120ms -> ~450ms, p95 ~1.8s -> ~4.5s, some 504s. Request IDs: req_20260320_84f2, req_20260320_84f7. They hit our hosted endpoint (model: rwd-3b-instruct) on us-west-2.

maya: thanks for the ping. is this across all regions or just us-west-2?

luis: they only reported us-west-2. said they started seeing it after a deploy around 08:58.

deployment-bot: deploy finished by alex to cluster us-west-2/runtime-pool-7 at 2026-03-20T08:58:14Z. commit: 7c9a2d4.

kyra: @maya @alex can you hook up traces for those request IDs? want to see if it's queuing in the frontend or kernel-level token generation. p95 jump suggests queuing/batching policy change or slow kernel.

alex: looking now — preliminary infra metrics show increased GPU utilisation on pool-7 around 08:58 and a spike in pending requests queued in the frontend service. No obvious OOMs or pod restarts.

maya: did we change batching config or default max_batch_latency in that deploy?

alex: yes — the PR toggled dynamic-batching tweak to reduce tail latency for long prompts. It changed default max_batch_latency_ms from 8 -> 12 for the text-generation route.

sam: that change was intended to help throughput. odd that p95 regressed for this customer. could be interplay with KV cache sizes or request length distribution.

nora: customer is on a dedicated reserved capacity plan (tier: enterprise-dedicated). SLA flagged. they want ETA and mitigation.

kyra: escalation: mark as high. immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the batching tweak for dedicated pools, 2) route Atrato to an alternate pool/region, 3) increase frontend workers temporarily. Which can we do fastest?

alex: fastest: spin up more frontend replicas and add a routing override for their tenant to another us-west-2 pool that didn't get the deploy. rollback takes ~20-30m to coordinate plus monitor.

maya: can we do a routing override? how many dedicated pools are compatible with rwd-3b-instruct in us-west-2?

alex: two other pools (pool-3, pool-9). pool-9 already at 70% util, pool-3 at 40%. Looks safe to route them to pool-3.

luis: customer prefers minimal disruption — would accept a short failover if it fixes latency. they asked for hourly updates.

kyra: I'm going to collect traces and check JVM/ephemeral queue times. @alex please start the routing override to pool-3 and bump frontend replicas by +3. I'll watch.

alex: started: running command:
```
./routingctl assign-tenant --tenant atrato --target-pool pool-3 --reason "latency regression triage"
kubectl scale deploy/frontend-usw2 --replicas=12 -n runtime
```

deployment-bot: routing change created (change_id rc-8812). frontend scaled event recorded.

kyra: traces show the bulk of time is spent in the batching window — requests are waiting ~9-11ms in queue now vs 2-3ms baseline. That aligns with max_batch_latency increase. The increased queue time pushes p95 up for short prompts.

maya: so the change helped throughput overall but penalized short, latency-sensitive requests. we need a smarter policy: dynamic per-tenant or short-prompt bypass.

sam: product question: is this behavior within expected tradeoffs? should we have feature flag per tenant for batch latency? Atrato is SLA-sensitive — we should offer an override.

nora: customer wants rollback unless we can guarantee latencies. they'd prefer an immediate fix over split testing.

maya: immediate plan — leave routing override to pool-3 (in progress). revert batching tweak for dedicated pools only, keep it for hosted multi-tenant but gated behind a feature flag. follow-up: implement per-tenant max_batch_latency config.

kyra: agree. I'll open an incident ticket and track mitigation steps. action items: kyra -> collect traces + confirm mitigation success; alex -> routing + scale; maya -> prepare rollback PR for dedicated pools; sam -> customer comms and SLA notes; luis/nora -> keep customer updated hourly.

luis: shared update to customer: "We detected the cause (batching tweak). We've routed your traffic to an alternate pool and are rolling back the change for dedicated customers. We expect p95 to return to normal within 15-30 minutes. We'll update you in 30 mins."

sam: internal priority: P1 for dedicated SLA impact. we'll schedule a 30min triage sync in 15min.

maya: rollback PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123 — marked for review and quick deploy to dedicated pools only.

alex: routing override complete, frontend replicas stable, gpu load on pool-3 increased but healthy. kyra, can you confirm p95 for Atrato?

kyra: post-mitigation p50 ~140ms p95 ~210ms p99 ~450ms for their sampled reqs. 504s dropped to zero. looks good.

nora: passing update to customer. they replied :thumbsup: and asked for postmortem and a permanent control to avoid regressions.

sam: agreed on next steps: 1) permanent per-tenant batch latency config 2) test matrix for batching change that includes short-prompt heavy workloads 3) rollout guardrails (canary % + latency SLO checks) 4) write KB for oncall to handle similar reports.

luis: thanks team. I'll keep this thread open for postmortem notes.

kyra: I'll attach relevant traces and metric dashboards to the incident ticket.

maya: postmortem owner: sam. target draft in 48h.

sam: noted. I'll own PM/triage and coordinate engineering writeup.

luis: (reacts :eyes:)

kyra: (reacts :zap:)

maya: leaving notes: consider adding an automated canary that runs short prompt latency profile after batching changes.

luis: closing customer loop: sent final note at 10:05 PST — customer confirmed stable.

sam: thanks all. we'll follow up with a formal postmortem and prioritization in the roadmap cadence.
